author: winnertrader
text:
Sorry to invade your journal Edge, but since we are talking about LS, I thought I might chime in.

On the Monthly chart it's ridiculously easy to draw RS lines from LS by
just scrolling to the left of the chart. Similarly, it is easy enough to
 mark out the hi's and lo's of the FL's that flank these very lines at
the first instance they form on the left (not from current PA).

When you get down to the weekly and daily, you don't have the luxury of
left of the chart... so in this case do we mark in the swap levels? I do
 find in my testing that it makes no difference whatsoever. The lines
that we mark in traditional fashion based on number of touches are just
as good as the ones you get by going to the extreme left of the chart.
The only question then is how to mark the limits of the FL's that flank
them because we have FL's in current price action as well as several in
the past.

I hope I'm making sense and not getting in over my head with this stuff.

Hi WinnerTrader I know it can be frustrating, but chin up my friend.
The QM Lite vids really helped me late last year. If I can give you some
 advice, I would say to focus on the best looking kinks which have a
whole lot of confluence. Remember that the best types of kinks also line
 up with LS as well. Play around with these areas mixed with good UFL
and LFLs and draw lines to see what happens in those areas. Refine until
 it becomes instinct
